subsystems.name: Neural signal acquisition
subsystems.role: reads electrical activity from the brain, either through implanted electrodes or from the scalp.
parts: intracortical microelectrode arrays or surface electrode grids

subsystems.name: Intent decoder
subsystems.role: turns raw voltage patterns into candidate intentions such as 'select', 'send', 'undo'.

subsystems.name: Confirmation and safety layer
subsystems.role: stops a brain signal from silently committing an irreversible action.
parts: deliberate confirm gesture or dwell timer

subsystems.name: Orchestration engine
subsystems.role: plans multi-step digital tasks and calls the right software tools in order.

subsystems.name: Integration layer
subsystems.role: connects the orchestrator to real systems.
parts: API connectors (email, CRM, file stores, ticketing)

subsystems.name: Feedback channel
subsystems.role: closes the loop so the user knows what was interpreted.

buildSteps.title: Choose the neural interface
buildSteps.detail: Decide between implanted arrays (high signal quality, surgery required) and non-invasive EEG (safe, but far lower information rate).

buildSteps.title: Record labelled training data
buildSteps.detail: A user performs or imagines defined actions — moving a cursor, attempting speech, counting — while neural activity and the intended label are logged together.

buildSteps.title: Train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Classifiers learn which patterns precede which intents; accuracy, latency and false-positive rate are measured, not assumed.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate per user and per session
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes drift and signals change day to day, so a short recalibration routine runs before each use.

buildSteps.title: Build the orchestrator
buildSteps.detail: A planning model is given a catalogue of tools and a policy for choosing and sequencing them, tested first on reversible actions like drafting or searching.

buildSteps.title: Add the confirmation layer
buildSteps.detail: Actions above a risk threshold require an explicit second signal or a dwell timer; everything is logged so a mistake can be traced and undone.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Feedback is returned to the user after each decoded intent so they can correct the system in real time.

buildSteps.title: Validate over months, not minutes
buildSteps.detail: Signal stability, decoder drift and user fatigue are measured across long sessions before any consequential task is allowed.

prerequisites.why: intracortical arrays lose signal over months to years as scar tissue forms; electrode counts and lifetimes are still the hard limit.

prerequisites.tech: Decoding of abstract intent, not just movement
prerequisites.why: cursor control and attempted-speech decoding work in small clinical studies, but open-ended goals like 'reconcile this account' are not yet decodable.
scalp EEG resolves roughly a few bits per minute of deliberate command, far too little to drive multi-step workflows.
software agents can chain API calls, but long-horizon correctness and permission handling remain unsolved.
brain signals are uniquely identifying and cannot be revoked like a password.

pathway.milestone: clinical BCIs let paralysed participants move a cursor, type and control robotic arms
pathway.unlocks: proof that movement and communication intent can be decoded reliably in a lab setting.

pathway.milestone: passive BCIs that read cognitive load, attention or error signals to adapt ordinary software
pathway.unlocks: neural input used as a weak hint that adjusts an interface, without controlling it.

pathway.milestone: research systems pairing decoded intent with software agents on narrow, reversible tasks
pathway.unlocks: evidence about which intents are decodable and which need explicit confirmation.

pathway.milestone: regulated orchestration of consequential workflows, with confirmation layers and audit trails
pathway.unlocks: assistive control of real work for people with severe motor impairment, and only then wider use.
